newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW-Polish NFI Hetman to hold onto its firms.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Polish NFI Hetman to hold onto its firms.

text.p: National Investmemt Fund (NFI) Hetman (No 15) in Poland's mass privatisation programme plans to hold most of the firms in its portfolio for the long term, the fund's president said on Wednesday.

"We might be the owners of the firms in the long term because of expected growth in the sectors in which they operate," Krzysztof Sedzikowski told Reuters, adding that the fund had concentrated on mineral and food firms.
He said firms in those two branches represented 19 percent and 15 percent respectively of the fund's portfolio and that Hetman sought to form a group of firms in the mineral sector.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
Sedzikowski said that among food producers Hetman was concentrating on meat firm Zaklady Miesne Ostroda-Morliny SA, which it planned to put on the bourse at the turn of the year.
He said the fund planned to buy firms outside the programme, including chipboard maker Zaklady Plyt Wiorowych w Wieruszowie SA, for which negotiations were underway.

"We plan to invest in the firm at Wieruszow -- it's a twin of Grajewo which is already in our portfolio, and in being an investor at Wieruszow we would have a strong competitive presence on the Polish market," Sedzikowski said.
He said the fund was mulling selling shares in about five of its firms to strategic investors, such as the Rudniki cement firm, in which Hetman held 60 percent after a capital increase.
Sedzikowski said foreign cement makers operating in Poland and elsewhere had expressed interest in Rudniki.
